app.name: sshud
overview.title: Machines
sort.name: Name
card.partialHint: Some metrics could not be read: {list}
hint.unreachable: Check that the machine is on and its network is up.
hint.timeout: The machine did not answer on its SSH port. Is it online, and is the port open?
hint.refused: Nothing is listening on the SSH port. Check the port number and that sshd is running.
hint.key: sshud could not read or create its own key in the data directory. Check the directory's permissions.
hint.auth: The key was not accepted. Check the user name and that sshud's line is in authorized_keys (Machines → Connect).
hint.hostkey: The machine presented a different host key than before. Confirm it was reinstalled before trusting it again.
retrust.title: Trust the new host key of {name}?
retrust.body: Only do this if you know the machine was reinstalled or its SSH host keys were regenerated. Otherwise someone may be intercepting the connection. Compare the new fingerprint with ssh-keygen -lf /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub on the machine.
hint.rejected: The forced command did not match. Authorize this machine again (Machines → Connect).
hint.unsupported: The probe output could not be read on this system.
hint.internal: Something went wrong inside sshud. See the server log.
empty.title: No machines yet
detail.noDocker: Docker is not installed, or this user cannot run docker ps.
manage.title: Machines
manage.name: Name
manage.deleteBody: sshud stops reading this machine and forgets its host key. Nothing changes on the machine itself.
manage.readOnly: Demo mode: the machine list is built in and cannot be changed.
manage.emptyBody: Add a Linux machine you can reach over SSH. sshud reads /proc with its own read-only key; nothing is installed on it.
empty.body: Add a Linux machine you can reach over SSH. Nothing is installed on it.
import.title: Import from ssh_config
import.label: Paste your ~/.ssh/config
import.help: Only Host blocks with HostName, User and Port are read. sshud always connects with its own read-only key.
import.none: No hosts found. Wildcard Host entries are only used as defaults.
strict.fromHelp: IP addresses or CIDR ranges the machine sees sshud connecting from, comma separated. Leave empty if unsure.
strict.reads: The line contains the whole read-only script. It reads files under /proc and /sys (temperatures, container usage), /etc/os-release, and the output of df, uname, getconf, who, ip addr and docker ps. It cannot write files or open a shell.
manage.fingerprintCheck: It should match ssh-keygen -lf /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub on the machine.
setup.title: Connect {name}
setup.intro: sshud reads this machine with its own key, which only works after one line is in the account's ~/.ssh/authorized_keys. sshud never touches your personal SSH keys.
setup.command: Run this on your own computer. It logs in with your own SSH key, as you normally would, and adds the line (replacing an older sshud line). sshud does not run it and never sees your key.
setup.line: Or append the line yourself to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys of the user above. Then press Test connection.
login.title: Log in
login.setupBody: This sshud has no password yet. The password protects the machine list and every number on the dashboard.
display.title: Display
outdated.title: This machine has an old authorized_keys line
outdated.body: sshud has a newer probe than the authorization on this machine, so some numbers may be missing. Open Machines, choose Connect for this machine and authorize it again.
outdated.short: The authorization on this machine is outdated; authorize it again from Machines → Connect.
stale.title: Machines with an outdated authorized_keys line: {n}
boot.once: Used once to authorize sshud (one restricted key line in authorized_keys), then discarded. sshud does not store your password or private key.
boot.manual: Rather not hand over credentials? Authorize manually
boot.done: {name} is connected. It now shows on the overview.
hint.credentials: The password or key was not accepted. Check the user name and try again.
hint.nopassword: This machine does not accept passwords. Paste a private key instead.
hint.passphrase: The passphrase does not unlock this private key.
hint.install: sshud could not write ~/.ssh/authorized_keys on the machine. Its error output is in brackets.
error.verify: Authorized, but sshud's key does not work
hint.verify: sshd may read keys from somewhere else (AuthorizedKeysFile) or ignore options in authorized_keys. Authorize manually instead.
